listing.singlePurpose: Show WebMCP activity on one selected tab and enforce one already approved synthetic lab action through a closed local policy.
listing.summary: See WebMCP activity and guard one exact synthetic practice action through a local connector.
listing.description: Local Guard is an experimental browser-owned heads-up display for the LeftOut WebMCP Security Lab. It observes Site Tool declarations only on a tab the person explicitly selects, distinguishes observed, protected, changed, and receipt states, and can relay one already approved synthetic action through a closed, document-bound, no-retry policy. It does not approve actions, invoke arbitrary tools, read full page content, or send data to LeftOut Security. Version 0.3.0 is an unsigned controlled-tester preview, not a production security guarantee.

permissions.name: activeTab
permissions.justification: After the person opens Local Guard, identify and bind only the selected top-level tab and document.

permissions.name: scripting
permissions.justification: Call the experimental page-scoped WebMCP inspection and one exact approved action in the selected tab's main world without reading general page content.

permissions.name: storage
permissions.justification: Retain the person's privacy choice, exact document pairing, one-use permit state, pending result delivery, and anti-replay tombstone in the local browser profile.

hostPermissions.justification: Reach only the default connector on this device during the developer preview.
Reach only the default localhost connector alias during the developer preview.
Reach only the approved fallback connector port on this device during the developer preview.
Reach only the approved localhost fallback connector alias during the developer preview.

remoteCode.declaration: No remotely hosted code is loaded or executed. All extension logic is packaged in the reviewed Manifest V3 archive.

categories.name: web_history
categories.detail: Only the origin and path of the tab the person explicitly selects.

categories.name: website_content
categories.detail: Only WebMCP declarations and the bounded result and receipt for one approved synthetic action; no general page text or forms.

categories.name: authentication_information
categories.detail: Short-lived connector challenge and session credentials generated for the local bridge; never a website password or cookie.

dataUse.retention: Pairing ends on disconnect, navigation, tab close, or consent withdrawal. Unconsumed permits are removed; consumed permit digests remain only until expiry to prevent replay. Local connector receipts remain until the user removes local runtime data.
